headline: Earnings dip on deal costs; balance sheet swells pre-close
summary_short: National Fuel Gas's quarter ended June 30, 2026 net income fell 7.5% y/y to $138.6M ($1.45 diluted EPS, -11.6% y/y) on CenterPoint Ohio deal costs and lower Upstream earnings, against roughly flat revenue of $537.5M (+1.1% y/y); cash jumped to $1,235.2M after a $1.5B debt issuance.
summary_long: Earnings fell $11.2M y/y to $138.6M as a swing to a $7.7M Corporate/All Other net loss — driven by $4.8M of CenterPoint Ohio integration costs, higher labor/legal costs, and new acquisition financing interest — and a $4.8M decline in Integrated Upstream and Gathering earnings (lower gas production, higher depletion and lease costs) outweighed higher Utility earnings and flat Pipeline and Storage results. Revenue was roughly flat y/y at $537.5M. On June 10, 2026 the company issued $1.5B of long-term notes to help fund the pending $2.62B CenterPoint Ohio acquisition (closing expected October 1, 2026), lifting cash to $1,235.2M and long-term debt to $3,567.4M; the $300M delayed-draw term loan was fully repaid. No forward guidance was given in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Earnings fell $11.2M y/y primarily from a swing to a loss in the Corporate/All Other category and lower earnings in the Integrated Upstream and Gathering segment.
Upstream and Gathering revenue fell $3.9M as a 7.3 Bcf production decline outweighed a $0.10/Mcf realized-price gain, offset by modest Utility and Pipeline and Storage rate-driven growth.

Corporate posted a $7.7M net loss (vs $0.7M loss y/y) on CenterPoint Ohio integration costs and new deal-financing interest; Upstream and Gathering earnings fell $4.8M on higher depletion and lease costs.
EPS fell more than net income (-11.6% vs -7.5% y/y) because diluted shares rose 5.0% y/y after the December 2025 equity issuance raised to help fund the pending acquisition.
Purchased-gas cost is highly seasonal for the Utility segment; the swing from the winter-heavy prior quarter to the low-demand summer quarter depresses this line q/q every year.
Cash surged mainly from $1.5B of long-term notes issued June 10, 2026 ($500M each at 4.75%, 5.05% and 5.50%) to prefund the pending CenterPoint Ohio acquisition, partly offset by a $300M redemption.
Driven by the same June 2026 $1.5B note issuance to finance the pending $2.62B CenterPoint Ohio acquisition, net of a $300M note redemption.
The $300 million delayed-draw term loan outstanding a year ago was repaid in January 2026.
